curatorBrief.title: Adventures with Short /a/
curatorBrief.intent: Welcome kindergarten learners to the world of the short /a/ vowel sound. Introduce the friendly sound /a/ as in 'apple' and 'cat', outline how we can listen for this sound in spoken words, and show how we snap letter sounds together like building blocks to read words like cat, bat, and jam.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Listen to and identify the short /a/ sound in spoken words.

components.title: Hear and Say the Short /a/ Sound
components.intent: Introduce the continuous short vowel sound /a/ as in 'apple' and 'alligator' with live-judged spoken direct instruction. Model the /aaa/ sound clearly, prompt kindergarteners to stretch and say /aaa/ out loud, and recognize the sound at the beginning of spoken words.

components.title: Short /a/ Sound Detective
components.intent: Guide kindergarteners to listen to spoken words and identify whether they begin or contain the short /a/ sound. Use engaging pictures and spoken prompts where learners match spoken words like 'ant', 'axe', and 'apple' to the /a/ sound.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Blend individual letter sounds together to read short a CVC words.

components.title: Slide and Blend: Short /a/ Words
components.intent: Demonstrate sound-by-sound blending of CVC words containing short a (such as 'c-a-t', 'm-a-p', 's-a-d'). Students tap each letter tile to hear each isolated sound, slide their finger across to blend them continuously, and see a vibrant reward illustration when successfully decoded.

components.title: Read the Word Aloud!
components.intent: Engage learners in live-judged direct instruction word reading. Students see printed short a CVC words (such as 'cat', 'fan', 'hat', 'bag'), sound them out, and read the entire word out loud into the microphone with instant tutor praise and gentle guidance.

components.title: Word Workout: Match and Read
components.intent: Provide capstone decoding practice where students read a printed short a CVC word and connect it to its matching picture, demonstrating both accurate decoding and early comprehension.

finalAssessment.title: Short /a/ Reading Celebration
finalAssessment.intent: Assess mastery across both objectives through spoken and picture-tap questions: identifying spoken words with the /a/ sound and selecting the correct image for a decoded short a CVC word.

problems.question: Which word has the short a sound?
problems.rationale: When we stretch out the word cat, we hear the short /a/ sound in the middle: /k/ /a/ /t/. Words like bed have the short /e/ sound, and pig has the short /i/ sound. Remembering the mouth opens wide for /a/ helps us pick cat!
problems.teachingNote: Have students place a hand under their chin or look in a mirror when making the short /a/ sound versus /e/ or /i/ to feel their jaw drop open wide.
successCriteria: Identify the short /a/ vowel sound in a CVC word
Distinguish the short /a/ sound from short /e/ and short /i/
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: What word do the sounds /k/ /a/ /t/ make?
problems.rationale: When you slide the sounds /k/, /a/, and /t/ together, they build the word cat. The middle sound is the short a vowel sound /a/, which is different from the /o/ sound heard in cot or the /u/ sound heard in cup.
problems.teachingNote: Have students place a hand on their chin or stretch their arms like a rubber band as they isolate the middle vowel sound /a/ to distinguish it from similar short vowels like /o/ and /u/.
successCriteria: Blend individual phonemes /k/, /a/, and /t/ into the spoken CVC word cat.
Distinguish the short a vowel sound from other short vowel sounds in CVC words.
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: What word do the sounds /k/, /a/, /t/ make?
problems.rationale: When you blend the sounds /k/, /a/, and /t/ together smoothly, they make the word cat. Listening carefully all the way to the final /t/ sound helps you choose cat instead of cap or can.
problems.teachingNote: Encourage learners to tap their arm from shoulder to wrist for each sound before sweeping their hand down to blend the whole word.
successCriteria: Blend individual phonemes /k/, /a/, and /t/ into a spoken CVC word.
Differentiate between CVC words with the same onset and vowel by identifying the final consonant sound.
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which word ends with the same sound as cat?
problems.rationale: Bat ends with the /t/ sound, just like cat! Even though pan and man have the same short a sound in the middle, they end with the /n/ sound. Listening all the way to the final sound helps us find words in the -at family.
problems.teachingNote: Pre-readers often notice the shared middle /a/ sound and think words like cat and pan match. Prompt students to punch out or tap the final sound to contrast /t/ in 'bat' with /n/ in 'pan'.
successCriteria: Identify the final consonant sound in a short a CVC word.
Distinguish words in the -at family from words in the -an family.
